confirmation.method: review coordinator attestation in the project chat
confirmation.scope: Both reviewers agreed with three full-text decisions, two revised title and abstract decisions, five retrieval holds and descriptive intake of the TAC surveillance report.
confirmation.note: Labels identify the two reviewer slots. Coordinator confirmed agreement in chat. Separate signed forms and individual appraisal judgments were unavailable.

reports.title: Altitude decompression sickness.
reports.locator: Lim et al., Case 2 and Figure 1, pp. 351-352
reports.reason: The authors considered DCS the most likely diagnosis for the Singapore trainee in Case 2. Preserve the existing chamber narrative and four-month recovery follow-up. Case 1 followed an aircraft exposure. The training risk denominator is unknown.

reports.title: [Hyperbaric oxygenation in altitude decompression sickness and lung barotrauma].
reports.reason: The initiating exposure setting and distinction between altitude DCS and lung barotrauma treatment remain unresolved.

reports.title: Altitude decompression sickness: hyperbaric therapy results in 145 cases.
reports.locator: Davis et al. p. 728, Table VIII, overall and inside-observer and student subtotals
reports.reason: Retain the secondary hyperbaric-treated surveillance and crude within-program role contrast. The page image gives 51,441 for 1974 high-altitude student exposures, consistent with the printed subtotals. The broader 145 treatment cases have a different scope. Hold pooling with overlapping USAF surveillance.

effects.risk_set: USAF operational chamber training exposures tabulated by Davis et al., Table VIII
effects.interval_method: Wald interval on log RR assuming independent person-exposures
effects.matching_or_clustering: Repeat attendance and chamber-session linkage unreported. Calculation ignores potential dependence.
effects.locator: Davis et al. p. 728, Table VIII, overall and inside-observer and student subtotals
effects.eligibility_reason: Treatment-defined endpoint differs from all-grade symptomatic DCS. The USAF surveillance risk set may overlap Bassett and TAC.

reports.title: [Pathogenesis and prophylaxis of decompression sickness in altitude fliers. I. Influence of hyaluronidase on duration of oxygen prebreathing].
reports.reason: The German publisher summary identifies albino rats in a pharmacological decompression study.

reports.title: Studies on the cause of pain in high altitude bends.
reports.locator: NLM citation and Bancroft BANC MSS 87/86 c, Series 1, carton 1, folder 16
reports.reason: The finding aid confirms an archival lead. Original clinical setting and outcomes await retrieval.

reports.title: A 4-year retrospective descriptive study on treatment outcomes of decompression illness patients in various hyperbaric chamber centers in Thailand.
reports.locator: Jittanonta et al., Methods and Table 3
reports.reason: All 178 selected DCI treatment cases belong to four diving categories, including one military diver. The source does not study operational altitude chamber training.

reports.title: [Dynamics of several indices of the enzyme-hormone status of the body after hypobaria and during decompression sickness].
reports.locator: NLM author abstract and animal indexing
reports.reason: Indexed laboratory evidence describes animals and enzyme and hormone outcomes. The translated title and abstract differ on the direction of pressure change.

reports.title: Altitude decompression sickness: hyperbaric therapy results in 145 cases
reports.locator: Ovid publisher record, Plast Reconstr Surg. 1978;61(5):803
reports.reason: Distinct Wood and Davis publication with a shared title. Authorized full text and its relationship to Davis 1977 await verification.

reports.title: Hypobaric decompression sickness
reports.locator: Wiley author abstract, seven-year RAAF experience
reports.reason: Eleven hospital-treated patients followed approximately 2,500 subject decompressions. Retain the approximate abstract result. Exact risk-set coverage, ascertainment and overlap with Point Cook and wider ADF surveillance await source review.

reports.title: The Effect of Gender on Susceptibility to Altitude Decompression Sickness.
reports.locator: NASA Human Integration Design Handbook bibliography, p. 573, ADA328256
reports.reason: The original technical report remains unavailable. Source population, denominator and comparability to later studies are unverified.

supplementary_intake.basis: Eight reported musculoskeletal bends cases among 6,913 aircrews exposed as printed. Person-exposure unit, follow-up and membership in the Davis and Bassett risk sets remain unresolved.
